title: Affine normal quotients and the geometry of their exact sequences
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All group schemes below are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$, and all subgroup schemes are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$. Let $N\subseteq G$ be normal. The fppf sheaf quotient $Q=G/N$ is represented by an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$. Here the fppf quotient is the sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/N(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras. The quotient homomorphism $q:G\to Q$ has scheme-theoretic kernel $N$ and is faithfully flat and finitely presented. It is an $N$-torsor, meaning that $(g,n)\mapsto(g,gn)$ induces an isomorphism $G\times_k N\simeq G\times_QG$. Quotient formation commutes with every field extension: $(G/N)_K\simeq G_K/N_K$, compatibly with the quotient maps. If $G$ is smooth (respectively geometrically connected), then $Q$ is smooth (respectively geometrically connected). If $S\subseteq Q$ is a closed subgroup, its inverse image $P=G\times_Q S\subseteq G$ fits into an exact sequence $1\to N\to P\to S\to1$, with $P/N\simeq S$; if $S$ is normal in $Q$, then $P$ is normal in $G$. If $N$ and $S$ are smooth and connected, then $P$ is smooth and connected. More generally inverse image along $q$ identifies subgroups of $Q$ with subgroups of $G$ containing $N$, preserving normal inclusions and their quotients: for $S_1\triangleleft S_0\subseteq Q$ and $P_i=q^{-1}(S_i)$, one has $P_0/P_1\simeq S_0/S_1$. Exactness here means exactness as fppf sheaves of groups; in particular the rightmost homomorphism is locally surjective for the stated coverings. Faithfully flat means that the induced map on affine coordinate algebras makes the target algebra a faithfully flat module over the source algebra.

source.place: Theorem 5.28 and Propositions 5.24--5.29, printed pp.104--105; Section 5(j), printed pp.116--118, for sheaf quotients; Proposition 1.62, printed p.24; Proposition 5.59, printed p.114; Theorem 5.55 (correspondence theorem), printed p.113. Field base change follows from the quotient torsor and its sheaf universal property.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-subgroup-representation-kernel] to obtain $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_{r,k}$ with kernel $N$. The coordinate presentation of $\mathrm{GL}_r$ has finitely many variables and one inverted determinant, so it is affine of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to factor $\rho$ as $G\xrightarrow{q}Q\hookrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_{r,k}$. Thus $Q$ is affine of finite type and $q$ is faithfully flat. The closed immersion is a monomorphism, so $\ker q=\ker\rho=N$ on every algebra, hence as schemes.

source.place: Proposition 5.18 and Corollary 5.19, p.103; Theorem 3.34, p.75.

proof.text: Write $B=k[Q]$ and $C=k[G]$, finite-type $k$-algebras by [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra]. The algebra $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. A finite list generating $C$ over $k$ also generates it over $B$, since $q$ is a $k$-map. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes $C$ finitely presented over $B$. For every $x:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Q$, put $A'=A\otimes_B C$. This is a faithfully flat, finitely presented $A$-algebra, and its canonical $C$-map gives a lift of $x$ to $G(A')$. Faithful flatness survives this base change by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change], and it implies surjectivity on spectra by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. Finite presentation survives base change directly by tensoring the finite generators and relations.

source.place: Propositions 5.24--5.27, p.105, with the explicit affine lift of Corollary 3.35, p.75; finite-presentation refinement of the flat covers.

proof.text: For any $k$-algebra $A$, $q(g)=q(h)$ if and only if $g^{-1}h\in N(A)$. The mutually inverse natural formulas $(g,n)\mapsto(g,gn)$ and $(g,h)\mapsto(g,g^{-1}h)$ therefore give the asserted torsor isomorphism and identify its identity fibre with $N$. Representable functors satisfy descent by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. The map $G(A)/N(A)\to Q(A)$ is injective, and the cover constructed in step 2 locally puts every section of $Q$ in its image. Hence its associated fppf sheaf is $Q$: local representatives glue uniquely since their images in $Q$ agree and equality of their cosets is already detected by the displayed kernel calculation. This is exactness with local, rather than pointwise, surjectivity.

source.place: Proposition 5.24, p.105; Sections 5(j)--5(m), especially 5.73 and 5.79, pp.118--120.

proof.text: For a field extension $K/k$, base change preserves faithful flatness and the finite presentation in step 2, and the formulas of step 3 give $G_K\times_K N_K\simeq G_K\times_{Q_K}G_K$. For every $K$-algebra $A$, the map $G_K(A)/N_K(A)\to Q_K(A)$ is thus injective and locally surjective by the same tensor-algebra cover. The sheaf argument of step 3 identifies $Q_K$ with $G_K/N_K$. Both identifications send the class of $g$ to $q_K(g)$, so this is the canonical comparison, compatible with the quotient maps. It applies to arbitrary, including inseparable, extensions.

source.place: Section 1(e), p.24, exactness under field extension; Proposition 5.24 and 5.73, universal-property argument.

proof.text: If $G$ is smooth over $k$, apply [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] to $G\xrightarrow{q}Q\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: steps 1--2 give precisely flatness, surjectivity and local finite presentation of $q$. This proves smoothness of $Q$ without assuming $N$ smooth. If $G_{\bar k}$ is connected, step 4 and surjectivity on spectra give a continuous surjection $G_{\bar k}\to Q_{\bar k}$. Its image is connected: a separation of the target into two nonempty clopen subsets would pull back to such a separation of the source. Thus $Q$ is geometrically connected.

For a closed subgroup $S\subseteq Q$, form $P=G\times_Q S$. The group operations restrict because the image of a product, inverse or identity lies in $S$ whenever the original images do. Affinely, if $S=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$, then $P=\operatorname{Spec}(C/JC)$, a closed subscheme of $G$ of finite type over $k$. The map $P\to S$ is the base change of $q$, hence faithfully flat and finitely presented; its kernel is $N$ and its torsor formulas are those of step 3. The same injective-coset and local-lift argument gives $P/N\simeq S$, and hence the asserted exact sequence.

source.place: Proposition 5.54 and Theorem 5.55, pp.112--113, inverse-image direction; 5.73, p.118.

proof.text: Conversely, let $H\subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup containing $N$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to $H\to Q$; let its closed image factor be $I\subseteq Q$. Its flat map $H\to I$ is finitely presented by step 2's finite-generator argument, applied to this factorization. Certainly $H\subseteq q^{-1}(I)$. If $g\in G(A)$ maps into $I(A)$, lift its image locally to $h\in H(A')$; then $g^{-1}h\in N(A')\subseteq H(A')$, so $g\in H(A')$. Membership in the closed subgroup descends: the local map into $H$ glues by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], since its composites into $G$ agree and $H\to G$ is a monomorphism. Hence $q^{-1}(I)=H$ as sheaves and schemes. The same local lifts show that the image of $q^{-1}(S)$ is exactly $S$. The two constructions are therefore inverse and preserve inclusions.

source.place: Proposition 5.54 and Theorem 5.55, pp.112--113; Theorem 3.34, p.75.

proof.text: Normality is preserved in both directions. If $S\triangleleft Q$, then $q(gpg^{-1})=q(g)q(p)q(g)^{-1}\in S(A)$ gives $q^{-1}(S)\triangleleft G$ on all algebras. Conversely, if $H\triangleleft G$, lift $x\in Q(A)$ and $y\in I(A)$ after a common fppf refinement to $g\in G(A')$ and $h\in H(A')$. Then $xyx^{-1}$ is locally the image of $ghg^{-1}\in H(A')$, so belongs to $I(A)$ by descent of membership. Common refinements are obtained by tensoring the two faithfully flat finitely presented algebras. This also proves normality for $P_1\subseteq P_0$ when $S_1\triangleleft S_0$.

source.place: Theorem 5.55, p.113, and sheaf correspondence 5.76, p.119.

proof.text: For $S_1\triangleleft S_0\subseteq Q$, use the quotient construction of steps 1--3 on $S_0,S_1$ and on $P_0,P_1$. The composite $P_0\to S_0\to S_0/S_1$ has kernel $P_1$ on every algebra. It is locally surjective: first lift a quotient section to $S_0$, then lift that section to $P_0$ after a further cover. Its associated coset sheaf is therefore $P_0/P_1$, by the argument of step 3, and is also $S_0/S_1$. This gives the claimed isomorphism, with both maps induced by $P_0\to S_0$.

Suppose now $N$ and $S$ are smooth. The group $N_S=N\times_k S$ is affine, smooth and finitely presented over $S$; smooth base change is [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and finite presentation is the finite polynomial presentation of step 2. Left multiplication makes the represented sheaf $P$ a left $N_S$-torsor: on the fppf cover $P\to S$, a chosen lift $p$ identifies a fibre with $N$ by $n\mapsto np$, with inverse $p'\mapsto p'p^{-1}$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-group-torsor-representability]. The representing scheme is the already constructed $P$, by uniqueness of representation, so $P\to S$ is smooth. Since $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, their composite is smooth: affine-locally this is composition of smooth ring maps [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], using the affine-local equivalence in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Proposition 1.62(a), p.24, written by local torsor trivializations.

proof.text: If also $N$ and $S$ are connected, [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] applied to the identity of $N$ makes $N$ connected after every field extension. For $s\in S$, let $F=P_s$ and choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(s)$. The faithfully flat finite-presentation map $P\to S$ gives a nonempty affine finite-type $F_\Omega$. A maximal ideal of its coordinate algebra gives a closed point, and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] makes it an $\Omega$-point $p$. The torsor formulas identify $F_\Omega$ with $N_\Omega$ by $n\mapsto np$, so $F_\Omega$ is connected. The map $F_\Omega\to F$ is surjective by faithful flatness of a field extension and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. Thus $F$ is connected by the separation argument of step 5. Since $P\to S$ is affine, flat and surjective, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-qc-surjective-quotient-map] gives the quotient topology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-connected-fibres-quotient-preimage-connected] to the closed connected subset $S$ of itself: $P$ is connected.

source.place: Proposition 5.59(a), p.114, via connected fibres; Corollary 1.32, p.16; Stacks Tag 0377 (lemma-connected-fibres-quotient-topology-connected-components).

proof_origin.place: Affine quotient construction of Proposition 5.18, Corollary 5.19 and Theorem 3.34; Propositions 5.24--5.27, Theorem 5.55, Propositions 1.62 and 5.59, with explicit fppf local-lift arguments of 5.73--5.79.
